intro: Today’s AI builds showcase new agents, local tools, and multimodal demos pushing practical applications forward.

picks.name: antirion
picks.what: One‑binary Rust AI gateway that routes, secures, budgets and observes every LLM call across OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock and more.
picks.why: Provides unified cost control and security monitoring for multi‑provider LLM usage, essential for production teams.
picks.signal: 229 stars since 17 Oct, written in Rust

picks.name: sideOS.ai
picks.what: Runs locally to provide dictation, meeting assistance and background tasks powered by AI.
picks.why: Enables businesses to deploy on‑device AI without cloud latency or data‑privacy concerns.

picks.name: MemT-1.0
picks.what: Open‑source library delivering long‑term memory and extended context for AI agents.
picks.why: Helps developers build agents that retain information across interactions, improving continuity.
picks.signal: 390 stars since 19 Oct, written in Python

picks.name: Wan2.2 14B Preview
picks.what: Generates a video from a single image guided by a text prompt.
picks.why: Demonstrates multimodal generation, turning static visuals into dynamic content with simple prompts.

picks.name: Corgi
picks.what: Terminal multiplexer that displays multiple AI agents’ activity streams and lets you switch between them.
picks.why: Improves ergonomics for power users juggling several agents, making monitoring seamless.

picks.name: Argus
picks.what: Open‑source security platform designed to protect against agentic attacks.
picks.why: Addresses emerging threats where AI agents could be exploited, offering a defensive layer for developers.

picks.name: Lampline
picks.what: Open‑source framework to build and test AI phone agents locally with an AI caller, no API keys required.
picks.why: Allows rapid prototyping of voice agents while avoiding external API costs and latency.
picks.signal: 171 stars since 19 Oct, written in Python
